How to Create a Meta Ads Account: The Definitive Step-by-Step Guide for Beginners

6 November 2026 · 11 min read

You already know that Facebook and Instagram ads can help businesses reach new customers, generate leads, and drive sales. But before launching your first campaign, you need more than an ad creative and a budget—you need the right Meta advertising account structure and business assets in place. In this guide, we'll explain how to create a Meta Ads account step by step, configure the essential settings, and prepare your account for your first campaign.

Key Takeaways

  • A Meta Ads account is used to organize campaigns, manage advertising activity, and handle billing across Meta's advertising ecosystem.
  • Meta advertising setup involves more than creating an ad account because Pages, business assets, permissions, payment settings, and tracking may also be required.
  • Business ownership and permissions should be configured correctly before campaigns are launched.
  • Currency and time zone settings should be reviewed carefully because they affect reporting and account administration.
  • Website tracking should be configured before conversion-focused campaigns when website actions are important to measurement.
  • The next step after setup is to connect assets, configure measurement, define campaign goals, and prepare your first campaign.

What Is a Meta Ads Account?

A Meta Ads account is the account used to organize advertising campaigns, manage billing, and run ads across Meta's available advertising platforms.

First, your ad account is where advertising activity is organized. It is used to create campaigns, manage ad spending, review performance, and access billing information.

For example, a D2C skincare brand may run separate campaigns for customer acquisition, retargeting, and product launches while managing the advertising activity through one or more ad accounts.

Meta's advertising ecosystem reaches billions of people across its Family of Apps. Meta reported approximately 3.60 billion Family daily active people in June 2026, demonstrating why properly structured advertising infrastructure matters for businesses using Meta's platforms. — Source: Meta, 2026

What Is the Difference Between a Meta Business Portfolio and a Meta Ads Account?

A Meta Business Portfolio and a Meta Ads account serve different purposes because the business environment manages assets and access, while the ad account is used for advertising activity and billing.

Moreover, a Meta Business Portfolio can help organize business assets such as Pages, Instagram accounts, people, permissions, and advertising accounts.

For example, a business can give an agency access to an ad account without sharing an employee's personal Facebook login.

Business-level access improves ownership, security, and account management.

Why Do You Need a Meta Ads Account to Run Facebook and Instagram Ads?

A Meta Ads account matters because it creates the structure required to manage campaigns, billing, permissions, and advertising assets.

First, correct account ownership protects your business from access problems. For example, if an employee leaves, you can remove their business access without transferring ownership of advertising assets.

Second, a properly configured account helps teams separate responsibilities. For example, an agency employee may receive advertising access without receiving full business administration permissions.

A properly configured Meta Ads account should have the correct business ownership, user permissions, payment settings, and connected advertising assets before campaigns are launched.

Meta reported that ad impressions across its Family of Apps increased 14% year over year in Q2 2026, while average price per ad increased 12%. — Source: Meta, 2026

How Do You Create a Meta Ads Account Step by Step?

Creating a Meta Ads account involves setting up the appropriate business structure, creating the ad account, configuring account settings, assigning permissions, and adding a payment method.

Before you begin, prepare the following:

  • A personal Facebook account for identity and access
  • Your business information
  • A Facebook Page, if applicable
  • An Instagram professional account, if applicable
  • A valid payment method
  • Access to your business website if you plan to run conversion campaigns

Step 1: Access Meta's Business Management Environment

Meta's business management environment is where you organize advertising assets, people, permissions, and business accounts.

First, sign in with the Facebook account that will have authorized access to the business. Then create or select the appropriate Meta Business Portfolio for your company.

For example, if you operate one D2C brand, create a clearly named business environment for that brand rather than mixing multiple businesses together.

[Insert image: Meta business management dashboard showing the Business Portfolio overview | Alt text: "Access Meta Business Portfolio for Meta Ads account setup"]

Step 2: Create a New Meta Ad Account

A new Meta ad account is created from the business settings area where advertising assets are managed.

Next, navigate to the advertising account section and select the option to add or create an ad account. Meta's interface labels can change, so focus on locating the Accounts or Ad Accounts section within business settings.

Then enter the required account details, including:

SettingWhat to Review
Ad account nameUse a clear business or brand name
Time zoneSelect the location used for reporting
CurrencyChoose the currency you plan to use
Business ownershipConfirm the correct business owns the account

Account settings should be reviewed carefully before confirmation because currency and time-zone decisions can affect reporting and administration.

[Insert image: Meta ad account creation screen showing account name, currency, and time zone | Alt text: "Create Meta Ads account with business settings"]

Step 3: Add People and Assign Permissions

Meta Ads permissions determine who can manage campaigns, billing, and account settings.

Moreover, you should assign access according to responsibility rather than giving every team member full administrator permissions.

For example, a performance marketer may need campaign access, while a finance team member may only need access to billing-related information.

Access control reduces unnecessary security risks and makes account ownership easier to manage.

Step 4: Add a Payment Method

A Meta Ads payment method is the billing method used to pay for advertising charges generated by your campaigns.

Next, open the billing or payment settings area and add the appropriate payment method available for your business location.

For example, a company should use a payment method controlled by the business rather than depending entirely on a departing employee's personal payment details.

[Insert image: Meta billing settings showing payment method setup | Alt text: "Add payment method to Meta Ads account billing"]

Step 5: Connect Your Facebook Page and Instagram Account

Connected business assets allow your Meta Ads account to use the correct identities and placements when creating advertisements.

First, add your Facebook Page and connect the relevant Instagram account through your business settings.

For example, a fashion brand running Instagram ads should ensure that the correct Instagram professional account is connected before launching campaigns.

Asset connections should be tested before advertising spend begins.

How Do You Set Up a Meta Ads Account Correctly After Creating It?

Correct Meta Ads account setup includes reviewing permissions, billing, connected assets, tracking, and account security before launching campaigns.

First, check that the correct people have access. Remove unnecessary administrators and avoid sharing personal passwords.

Second, review your connected assets, including:

  • Facebook Page
  • Instagram account
  • Ad account
  • Website tracking setup
  • Payment method

Website tracking configuration should be completed before running conversion-focused Meta advertising campaigns when businesses need to measure actions taken on their website.

For example, an e-commerce brand running purchase campaigns should configure its website measurement setup before spending heavily on optimization campaigns.

[Insert image: Meta Events Manager showing website events and tracking status | Alt text: "Configure Meta conversion tracking for website campaigns"]

What Tools Should You Use for Meta Ads Account Setup?

Meta advertising tools help businesses manage campaigns, assets, tracking, and competitive research after the ad account has been created.

Meta Ads Manager

Meta Ads Manager is the primary tool used to create, manage, and analyze advertising campaigns.

For example, you can use it to review campaign delivery, budgets, audiences, creative performance, and conversion results.

[Insert image: Meta Ads Manager campaign dashboard showing campaign performance | Alt text: "Manage Meta Ads campaigns in Meta Ads Manager"]

Meta Events Manager

Meta Events Manager is used to manage and review website and event measurement configurations.

For example, a D2C brand can use event data to understand actions such as product views, add-to-cart activity, and purchases.

Meta Ad Library

Meta Ad Library is a free research tool that allows users to review active ads from advertisers across Meta's platforms.

For example, you can study competitor messaging, creative formats, offers, and campaign angles before developing your own ad concepts.

Competitive research improves creative decisions when it inspires original strategy instead of copying advertisements.

[Insert image: Meta Ad Library showing competitor advertising examples | Alt text: "Research competitor Meta ads in Meta Ad Library"]

What Should You Do After Creating a Meta Ads Account?

The next step after creating a Meta Ads account is to prepare your measurement, objectives, audience, creatives, and test budget before launching campaigns.

First, define what you want the campaign to achieve. For example, an e-commerce business may focus on purchases, while a service business may focus on qualified leads.

Next, follow this preparation checklist:

  1. Configure website tracking.
  2. Connect Facebook and Instagram assets.
  3. Choose the appropriate campaign objective.
  4. Research your target audience.
  5. Prepare multiple creative variations.
  6. Set an initial testing budget.
  7. Launch the campaign and monitor results.

Campaign optimization starts with accurate measurement and clear objectives.

What Are the Next Steps for Building a Successful Meta Ads Account?

The best next step is to treat your Meta Ads account as long-term advertising infrastructure rather than simply a tool for launching one campaign.

First, establish clear naming conventions if you manage multiple campaigns or accounts. For example, use consistent names based on brand, country, objective, and campaign type.

Second, review account access regularly. For example, remove former employees and agency users who no longer require access.

Third, monitor campaign performance using meaningful business metrics rather than focusing only on clicks. Meta reported $60.8 billion in revenue in Q2 2026, up 28% year over year, underlining the scale and competitiveness of its advertising ecosystem. — Source: Meta, 2026

Conclusion

Creating a Meta Ads account correctly is the foundation for secure, measurable, and scalable Meta advertising.

First, create the appropriate business structure and ad account. Then configure your currency, time zone, permissions, billing, and business assets.

Next, connect website tracking before launching conversion-focused campaigns. This setup can help you make better advertising decisions because your campaigns are built on clearer ownership and measurement.

A strong Meta Ads account structure makes campaign management easier before advertising budgets become larger.

Take the time to review your setup before launching your first campaign. Once the foundation is correct, you can focus on the activities that actually drive growth: audience research, creative testing, campaign optimization, and conversion improvement.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. Can I create a Meta Ads account without a Facebook Page?

You can create business advertising infrastructure without necessarily using a Page for every initial setup action, but most businesses will need appropriate connected identities and assets when running Facebook and Instagram ads.

For example, connect the business assets you plan to advertise from before creating campaigns.

2. How do I add a payment method to my Meta Ads account?

You can add a payment method through the billing or payment settings associated with your advertising account.

For example, choose a business-controlled payment method and ensure authorized finance team members can manage billing when necessary.

3. Can I have more than one Meta Ads account?

Businesses may be able to manage multiple advertising accounts depending on their Meta business structure, account status, and available permissions or limits.

For example, an agency may manage separate client advertising accounts rather than mixing multiple client budgets into one account.

4. Why is my Meta Ads account not working?

A Meta Ads account may have access, billing, policy, verification, asset, or account-status issues that prevent normal advertising activity.

For example, review your billing status, permissions, connected assets, and account notifications before attempting to create a campaign.

5. Should I set up website tracking before running Meta Ads?

Yes, website tracking should be configured before conversion-focused campaigns when website actions are important to campaign measurement.

For example, an e-commerce store should validate important customer actions before optimizing campaigns toward purchases.
